title: How can I read /etc/resolv.conf file?
body:
CoreDNS do not have tools, so I can read file:
- do not have shell (sh, bash, etc) (kubectl exec -it coredns.... -- /bin/sh)
- do not have 'cat' or similar to view contents
- do not have tools to copy files (e.g. kubectl cp ...)
- do not have package manager (e.g. apt), so I can't install tools

So how I can view contents of the file inside CoreDNS container?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
It is inside Azure AKS cluster. And if I try to use ephemeral container:
error: ephemeral containers are disabled for this cluster (error from server: "the server could not find the requested resource").

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Can you create a test pod with same [dnsPolicy/dnsConfig](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.19/#poddnsconfig-v1-core) as CoreDNS. Then checking resolv.conf in test pod should help?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Generally in Kubernetes the coredns Pod resolv.conf is the same as the one on the node the pod runs on.  That’s the default behavior of kubelet, but kubelet can optionally be configured to set up pods with same dnsPolicy as coredns with a different resolv.conf.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Is anyone knows how frequently it is sync with node? (if resolv.conf is changed on node, how long it will take to refresh in container, or this is only done on creation Container and later I need to rebuild container if I want to update?)

That is managed by kubelet, a Kubernetes component we don't maintain here.  I _suspect_ (though I do not know for sure) that kubelet just does this at container creation time. IMO, the resolv.conf file was designed to be somewhat static, not a dynamic configuration - changes in the upstream nameserver list are expected to be relatively uncommon.

Regardless, CoreDNS's _forward_ plugin only reads the resolv.conf at start up, and _reload_ plugin does not monitor the file if it changes.

So, for multiple reasons, you'll need to restart the Pod when resolv.conf changes.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> ... Azure AKS. I change only ConfigMap ...

Given the restrictions imposed by AKS, I don't see a solution. Even adding a sidecar to the Pod that monitors the file is not possible if you are not allowed to change the Deployment.

I think the best you can do is infer the configured upstreams from the forward plugin's coredns_forward_requests_total metric (which holds a count of requests for each configured nameserver).
